name: justaluckydude
archetype: In-play sports taker reacting to scoring plays
headline: Buys the side a scoring play just helped, within 0-10 seconds of the play, across NFL, college football, NBA, MLB and NHL moneylines, spreads and totals. The reaction is real and matches the wallet, but a public-data version is not significantly profitable, a 5-second delay removes most of the edge, and the wallet's own edge is decaying.
mechanism: All 200 sampled fills are taker fills (on-chain) and 99.6% happen after game start. Against ESPN play-by-play wall-clock times, the wallet's fills spike from a baseline of ~300 per 5-second bin to 1,274 in the first 5 seconds after a scoring play and 797 in the next 5, with no rise before plays. Within 20 seconds after a play, 95% of its buys favour the scoring side (other takers: 62%). These reactive trades are about 30% of its fills; the rest are not explained by scoring plays.

roc.detail: peak capital at risk $507k; 30-day PnL $139k; 27% per month

match.detail: partial: direction after scoring plays 95% vs 62% for other takers, permutation p=0.005 (86 held-out games), but this explains only ~30% of fills

backtest.detail: REACT(D=0s, W=20s) on 86 held-out games: +3.8% on $1.26M traded, per-game p=0.21; wallet's own fills on the same games +3.2%, p=0.25

replicable.detail: reacts 0-10 s after the play's wall clock, faster than public feeds or broadcast; +5 s delay: +1.0%, p=0.41

persistence.detail: last 30 days not significant (p=0.13); daily mean fell from $9.1k to $4.6k; negative trend p=0.004

reasons: The reverse-engineered reaction rule matches only the ~30% of fills that follow scoring plays.
The rule is not significantly profitable on 86 held-out games (p=0.21), even with zero added delay.
Speed is the edge: trades land within 0-10 s of the play; 5 s slower leaves +1.0% (p=0.41).
The wallet's own PnL has a significant negative trend (p=0.004) and its last 30 days are not significant.
